problem:
Consider the solution curves of the differential equation ${x}^{2}{y}^{′}={e}^{y}.$ Which of the following points are stationary points of their respective solution curve?

- $(1,0)$
- $(2,-2)$
- $(e,1)$

choices.value: None of the points are the stationary points of the function

feedback.problem:
Consider the solution curves of the differential equation ${y}^{2}{y}^{′}=y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Which of the following are stationary points of their respective solution curve?

- $(\pi ,1)$
- $(\pi ,-1)$
- $(0,-1)$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a stationary point of $y(x)$ is a point $x=c$ in the domain of $y$ such that ${y}^{′}(c)=0.$ 

First, we make ${y}^{′}$ the subject of the equation.

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}{y}^{′}=y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,⟹\,{y}^{′}=\frac{y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the coordinates of our points into the differential equation and calculate the value of the derivative: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{{y}^{′}|}_{(\pi ,1)} & ={(\frac{y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{y}^{2}})|}_{(\pi ,1)} \\  & =\frac{(1)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{(1)^{2}} \\  & =0\,✓ \\ {{y}^{′}|}_{(\pi ,-1)} & ={(\frac{y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{y}^{2}})|}_{(\pi ,-1)} \\  & =\frac{(-1)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =-2 \\  & \ne 0\,\times  \\ {{y}^{′}|}_{(0,-1)} & ={(\frac{y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{y}^{2}})|}_{(0,-1)} \\  & =\frac{(-1)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
